voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Tucson, two thousand nine. A lab tests four slivers of vellum from a book that has never been deciphered.
One theory said the dealer who bought it in nineteen twelve, Wilfrid Voynich, had faked it himself.
The slivers came from four different pages. All four dated the skin to the early fourteen hundreds.
That dates the skin, not the writing. But nothing in the inks or paints was out of place for that time.
A modern fake now looks unlikely. Yet no one has proved what a single word of it says.
